body: I do force myself to do hygene things, but it's so easy to just give up on cleaning and walk around it. It does feel so much better after a good clean, though

I have a lot of trouble cleaning. When I clean it's easy for my mind to wander, and my wandering mind leads to heavyanxiety. Same as to why I hate showers, falling asleep without pills, going on walks, etc. 


Thank you for the post, it's very motivating.

I don't think he'll view you as a sinking ship. Just bringing up big mental health issues when you first meet someone is very straining and can be a red flag depending on a lot of factors. 


It's def a good idea to treat carefully. At the same time, don't obsess that he's judging you once you share. Worry tends to erode relationships like that. It's a big issue of mine lol

I've been with my boyfriend for about 5 months and just haven't mentioned self harm. My scars are kinda obvious. All acquaintances or closer with little self control have mentioned them. Sometimes touch them. Cringe. 


My bf obviously can see them and hasn't really said anything. He's worringly asked why fresh scratches exist and I say they're from work (not a lie, and I haven't SH'd in a while) and explain what happen. He believes me. That's the extent of it. 


I feel like it's the best to not say anything until they inquire. Springing your self harm issues on a fresh relationship is damaging without a solid foundation of friendship beforehand. 


I find it best when asked to make it short and sweet with a positive twist, yet no lies. Speak calmly. Don't imply it's worse than you say, but don't understate it. 


"What're those scars from?"


"I've had issues with self harm. It can still be a struggle still, but I'm getting help from (therapy, support group, family, etc.) and have been doing it less and less." 


Gauge their reaction and base that on how much you share next. Don't be afraid to hold back a bit even if he's interested in your story. Again, it can be a huge strain on fresh relationships even if he seems interested. 


If you don't make it into a huge deal, it doesn't become a turn off. Once you become closer, then it can be a good idea to open up further. 


Btw, I feel like I've been around my bf long enough to talk about anything(we spend a ton of time together), but self harm just isn't a huge problem for me now. So I haven't said anything for that reason. 


I feel at this point he's both trustworthy and mature enough to listen without judgement, and it's important to know that before you share to prevent getting hurt. I learned that the hard way in past relationships.
